title: Aurora escalation postmortem follow-up
next_steps: Redwood to share updated incident timeline doc and patch notes
Aurora to run 24h smoke test on Dedicated pool and report errors
Schedule follow-up runbook review with Aurora SREs (week of 2026-09-22)
action_items: Priya Nair: push autoscaler hotfix to staging and validate metrics (due 2026-09-20)
Marcus Chen: share revised postmortem deck and incident timeline (due 2026-09-18)
Lena Ortiz: confirm stakeholders for runbook sign-off and provide availability (due 2026-09-21)
Tom Becker: send list of compliance questions about log retention/KMS configurations (due 2026-09-19)
summary: Follow-up after last week's outage that impacted Aurora's HL7 ingestion pipeline on Redwood Dedicated. We reviewed root cause (autoscaler race + KV cache invalidation during rollout), mitigations already deployed (autoscaler guardrails, cache warmup, canary routing), and next steps for runbook and longer-term reliability improvements.
topics: incident timeline; root cause analysis; mitigations deployed (hotfixes); runbook and on-call changes; security/compliance questions; next validation steps and SLO adjustments
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're doing a 30-40 minute follow-up on last Thursday's incident. I know folks are busy so we'll get straight to the timeline.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We'll just give quick context from our side then want to go over the fixes and tests.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Quick heads up - transcription might drop some product names, 'Red wood' sometimes shows up, sorry in advance.
[00:28] Raj Patel: No worries. So we had a consistent spike in tail-latency and then the HL7 ingestion batch started failing about 02:14 UTC, right?
[00:36] Marcus Chen: Correct, our postmortem timeline shows autoscaler attempted to deprovision a node during a model rollout which caused a KV cache mismatch and then many requests hit cold cache which amplified CPU use.
[00:49] Maya Gonzalez: There was also an unlucky overlap with our scheduled data backfill job, so load was higher than expected. The combination pushed the dedicated pool over the threshold.
[01:05] Priya Nair: To be precise, two things aligned: the autoscaler had an aggressive scale-in threshold and the rollout created a transient incompatibility between kernel selection and cached KV entries. That caused increased latency and then retries flooded the service.
[01:24] Tom Becker: From security lens, we flagged that audit logs were incomplete for the 15 minutes window - we want confirmation logs are now durable and sent to our SIEM.
[01:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, Marcus, can you cover the mitigations you pushed yesterday?
[01:41] Marcus Chen: Sure. We deployed three immediate mitigations: 1) autoscaler guardrails to prevent scale-in during rollouts, 2) cache warmup during canary rollout so new instances pre-populate KV cache, and 3) routing fallback to run on a compatible model variant when node capacity is low.
[02:02] Raj Patel: We saw the error rate drop after the guardrails were active, approx from 12% to under 1.5% within 10 minutes. Logs attached in the deck Marcus shared.
[02:18] Priya Nair: One note - the cache warmup is conservative right now because we didn't want to increase memory footprint too much. We can tune based on your traffic profile.
[02:29] Lena Ortiz: That's fine, we prefer reliability over memory until this stabilizes.
[02:35] Maya Gonzalez: On runbook items, our on-call playbook assumed that model rollouts were safe during low traffic windows; evidently not. We need a clearer gating and pre-rollout checklist.
[02:48] Jordan Lee: Agreed. Action item - revised runbook and rollout gating. Marcus will own the runbook draft and we'll iterate with Aurora.
[02:56] Priya Nair: Also, for longer-term we suggested an autoscaler rewrite to handle rollout-awareness and avoid race conditions - that's on our roadmap under Optimize / autoscale improvements.
[03:10] Raj Patel: Timeline for that rewrite? Not urgent if guardrails hold, but want to understand risk window.
[03:16] Priya Nair: We estimate a Q4 timeline for major autoscaler improvements; we can prioritize a smaller patch sooner that adds rollout state checks - that could be a couple weeks.
[03:28] Tom Becker: For audit logs - did the fix ensure logs are appended to the KMS-backed S3 bucket? We have retention and encryption queries.
[03:36] Marcus Chen: Yes, we confirmed with infra that missing logs were because a temporary sink outage; we've re-published and validated parity. All logs are encrypted with customer-managed keys where configured. We'll send the validation report.
[03:48] Lena Ortiz: Good. Also we had questions about data residency and whether Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 are fully isolated - for compliance.
[03:56] Jordan Lee: They are; dedicated pools are single-tenant VPC and we support KMS/HSM integration for key control. We'll include the architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[04:08] Maya Gonzalez: There were a few unclear transcribed terms in Marcus' deck - like 'KV cache' showing up as 'K V cash' - but we understood.
[04:16] Priya Nair: Heh, transcription filter strikes again.
[04:20] Raj Patel: On SLOs: should we tighten our latency SLOs or add additional safety margins? We had a 95th at 250ms and the tail spiked.
[04:31] Jordan Lee: Recommendation - maintain current SLOs but add automatic temporary throttling and circuit-breaker when error rate crosses threshold, with alerting to both Aurora and Redwood. This reduces blast radius.
[04:46] Lena Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. For the pilot we want the temporary throttling behavior documented and approved.
[04:53] Marcus Chen: We'll include the throttle thresholds and the circuit-breaker rules in the runbook.
[04:59] Tom Becker: A final compliance ask - can you provide the SOC2 section showing change management and rollout approvals?
[05:07] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 artifact and our internal change policy notes.
[05:12] Maya Gonzalez: Thanks. Ok quick recap and next steps?
[05:16] Jordan Lee: Recap - root cause autoscaler scale-in during rollout + cache invalidation; mitigations deployed (guardrails, cache warmup, canary routing); longer-term autoscaler improvements on roadmap; runbook and SOC2 artifacts to be shared.
[05:31] Marcus Chen: Actionables: hotfix validation, runbook draft, logs validation, and schedule runbook workshop.
[05:40] Raj Patel: We'll run a 24-hour smoke test on the Dedicated pool starting Monday and feed results back.
[05:46] Jordan Lee: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and incident timeline in next 24 hours.
[05:52] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.
[05:54] [meeting ends]
